meta.scene_summary: We are building the future on top of legacy code, stolen data, and a growing stack of subscription fees.

cooking.headline: Microsoft finally admits C++ is the aging parent you keep in the house for sentimental reasons.
cooking.summary: Rust has officially reached Tier-1 status at Microsoft, joining C# and C++ in the inner circle of languages. It's the ultimate validation for a language that spent years being the 'too cool for school' kid in the corner of the repo.
cooking.plain_english: Microsoft has officially elevated Rust to a top-tier programming language, meaning it will receive the same level of support and investment as the company's primary development languages.

cooking.headline: Bending Spoons is buying Miro, so prepare for your infinite canvas to get a subscription fee increase.
cooking.summary: Bending Spoons is dropping over a billion dollars on a digital whiteboard company that we all use to draw boxes during meetings. It's the ultimate corporate upgrade: paying a premium price for the privilege of moving sticky notes around a screen.
cooking.plain_english: The software company Bending Spoons has agreed to purchase the online whiteboard and collaboration platform Miro for 1.355 billion dollars.

cooking.headline: Cognition dropped SWE-2, because apparently, the software engineering job market wasn't chaotic enough.
cooking.summary: Cognition's new model is here to compete with the latest industry giants, proving that the shelf life of a 'state-of-the-art' AI is currently shorter than a carton of milk. It's great to see more competition, provided the model doesn't start hallucinating entire microservice architectures at 3 AM.
cooking.plain_english: The AI company Cognition has released a new software engineering model called SWE-2 that is designed to perform at the same level as other top-tier AI coding assistants.

cooking.headline: Apple finally invented the folding phone, just in time for the rest of the industry to be bored of them
cooking.summary: Apple has officially announced the iPhone Duo, proving that if you wait long enough, even a folding screen becomes a revolutionary innovation. It is the tech equivalent of showing up to a party two hours late and acting like you are the guest of honor.
cooking.plain_english: Apple has announced its first foldable smartphone, the iPhone Duo.

cooking.headline: Blizzard devs finally unlocked the 'Union' achievement after years of raid-boss management.
cooking.summary: After years of crunch culture and internal chaos, Blizzard workers have officially ratified a historic union contract. It turns out that even the most legendary developers eventually realize that 'passion' doesn't pay the mortgage.
cooking.plain_english: Blizzard employees have successfully negotiated and signed their first formal labor union agreement.

cooked.headline: The CEO who spent all week fighting on Twitter just got sent to his room by the board.
cooked.summary: Matt Mullenweg's public crusade against WP Engine has officially spiraled into a forced sabbatical from his own company. It turns out that when you treat your business disputes like a reality TV show, the producers eventually decide to cut your mic.
cooked.plain_english: The board of directors at Automattic has required CEO Matt Mullenweg to take a leave of absence.

cooked.headline: Shopify realized that 'write once, run anywhere' actually means 'debug twice everywhere'
cooked.summary: Shopify is ditching React Native to go back to fully native code after years of trying to bridge the gap. It turns out that when you want a high-performance app, the cross-platform bridge is just a very expensive way to find out you should have used Swift and Kotlin from the start.
cooked.plain_english: Shopify is moving its mobile application development away from the React Native framework to use native programming languages instead.

cooked.headline: Amazon is bringing banner ads to your AI chatbot because the internet wasn't cluttered enough already.
cooked.summary: Amazon is testing ad services within ChatGPT, ensuring that your quest for knowledge is interrupted by a sponsored suggestion for a toaster. It is a bold strategy to turn a sophisticated LLM into a high-tech version of a junk mail flyer.
cooked.plain_english: Amazon is testing a feature that allows advertisements to appear within interactions on the ChatGPT platform.

cooked.headline: OpenAI really wants to train on your data, even if you say no
cooked.summary: OpenAI keeps toggling your 'allow training' setting back to 'on' like a landlord entering your apartment to rearrange the furniture. It turns out the biggest threat to your privacy isn't a hacker, but a UI that treats your opt-out preferences as mere suggestions.
cooked.plain_english: Users have reported that OpenAI repeatedly resets their privacy settings to allow the company to use their data for training artificial intelligence models after they have previously opted out.

cooked.headline: OpenAI's latest 'breakthrough' might just be your stolen DMs
cooked.summary: Researchers are pointing out that OpenAI's impressive new capabilities look suspiciously like they were fed a diet of private user conversations. It is the tech equivalent of a student claiming they wrote a brilliant essay while ignoring the fact that they clearly copy-pasted the entire thing from a classmate.
cooked.plain_english: A researcher has alleged that OpenAI used private user conversations to train its models and then presented the resulting performance improvements as a technological breakthrough.
